subject: pathology
title: Pathological Calcification, Dystrophic Deposition, and Psammoma Bodies

steps.tx: The abnormal tissue deposition of calcium salts together with smaller amounts of iron, magnesium, and other mineral salts constitutes pathological calcification. When mineral precipitation occurs locally in dying, necrotic, or damaged tissues despite completely normal circulating serum calcium and phosphate levels, the process is designated **dystrophic calcification**.
steps.say: Dystrophic calcification deposits calcium salts in damaged or necrotic tissue despite normal serum calcium.

nodes.label: Cellular Necrosis Generates Abundant Membrane Phospholipid Fragments
Negatively Charged Phosphate Groups Electrostatically Chelate Calcium
Membrane-Associated Phosphatases Cleave Inorganic Phosphate Groups
Calcium Phosphate Nucleates into Insoluble Hydroxyapatite Crystals

steps.tx: Dystrophic calcification initiates on membrane fragments within dead cells, where phosphatases generate concentrated phosphate ions that bind ambient calcium. Over time, the amorphous calcium phosphate precipitate organizes into structural **hydroxyapatite crystal lattices**, causing progressive hardening and functional stenosis of affected heart valves and atheromatous arterial plaques.
steps.say: Amorphous calcium phosphate precipitates on necrotic membranes, organizing into rigid hydroxyapatite.

left.title: Dystrophic Calcification
points: Occurs in dead, dying, degenerating, or necrotic tissues
Normal serum calcium and normal phosphate metabolism
Initiates locally within membrane-bound vesicular fragments
Examples: calcific aortic stenosis, tuberculous caseum, atheromas

right.title: Metastatic Calcification
points: Occurs in normal, healthy, non-injured tissues throughout body
Driven by sustained systemic hypercalcaemia or hyperphosphataemia
Predilects alkaline tissues with active acid excretion (lungs, stomach, kidneys)
Examples: primary hyperparathyroidism, bone metastases, vitamin D toxicity

steps.tx: In contrast to dystrophic deposition, calcification occurring in normal, uninjured tissues secondary to persistent systemic hypercalcaemia represents metastatic calcification. Characteristically, **metastatic calcification sites** involve internal organs that actively excrete acid, where local tissue alkalinization promotes calcium phosphate precipitation, predominantly affecting gastric mucosa, alveolar septa, and renal tubular basements.
steps.say: Metastatic calcification deposits calcium in healthy alkaline tissues due to systemic hypercalcaemia.

nodes.label: Gastric, Alveolar, and Renal Tissues Excrete Acid, Elevating Local pH
Alkaline Environment Drastically Lowers Calcium Phosphate Solubility
Metastatic Hydroxyapatite Crystallizes Across Delicate Basement Membranes

steps.tx: Common clinical causes of metastatic calcification include primary hyperparathyroidism, parathyroid-hormone-related peptide secretion by squamous cell carcinomas, osteolytic skeletal metastases, vitamin D intoxication, and chronic kidney disease. In chronic renal failure, phosphate retention drives secondary hyperparathyroidism and elevates the **calcium-phosphate solubility product** above seventy.
steps.say: Metastatic calcification occurs when hypercalcaemia or renal phosphate retention exceeds the solubility product.

left.title: Hypercalcaemia Drivers
points: Primary hyperparathyroidism from solitary parathyroid adenoma
Humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy via PTHrP secretion
Widespread osteolytic bone metastases from breast or lung cancer
Extra-renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity in sarcoid granulomas

right.title: Hyperphosphataemia Drivers
points: Chronic kidney disease with decreased phosphate filtration
Secondary hyperparathyroidism attempting to excrete retained phosphate
Elevated calcium x phosphate ion product exceeding 60-70 mg2/dL2
Calciphylaxis: lethal metastatic calcification of cutaneous arterioles

steps.tx: Under light microscopy, dystrophic calcium deposits can organize into concentric, lamellated, spherical basophilic calcifications resembling tiny microscopic pearls. Known as **psammoma bodies**, these structures represent successive waves of mineral deposition around single necrotic tumor cells, providing a distinctive diagnostic histological hallmark in specific neoplasms.
steps.say: Psammoma bodies are concentric, lamellated calcified spheres formed around dying neoplastic cells.

vis.caption: Whorled arachnoid meningothelial proliferation showing abundant concentric basophilic psammoma bodies.
vis.alt: Histological section of meningioma demonstrating abundant calcified psammoma bodies

steps.tx: The classic tumors and lesions known for displaying prominent psammoma bodies are summarized by the medical mnemonic PSaMMoma. These include papillary thyroid carcinoma, serous papillary cystadenocarcinoma of the ovary, meningioma, and malignant mesothelioma, where the **concentric calcified rings** stain dark purple-blue with hematoxylin.
steps.say: Psammoma bodies classically occur in papillary thyroid cancer, serous ovarian cancer, and meningioma.

vis.caption: Papillary fronds displaying ground-glass nuclei and concentric basophilic psammoma calcifications.
vis.alt: Papillary thyroid carcinoma histology exhibiting laminated psammoma bodies

steps.tx: On standard histological sections stained with hematoxylin and eosin, calcium salts appear as intensely basophilic, amorphous, granular or clumped deposits. Pathologists confirm calcium composition using the **von Kossa silver stain**, which reacts with phosphates to turn black, or Alizarin Red S, which binds directly to calcium to form an orange-red lake.
steps.say: Von Kossa stain reacts with phosphate to turn calcium deposits black, while Alizarin Red turns red.

left.title: Von Kossa Silver Reaction
points: Relies on photochemical reaction with calcium-bound phosphate ions
Silver cations replace calcium in hydroxyapatite crystals
Ultraviolet reduction precipitates visible black metallic silver
Standard histological method for demonstrating microcalcifications

right.title: Alizarin Red S Staining
points: Directly chelates ionized and crystalline calcium cations
Forms birefringent, bright orange-red insoluble coordination lake
High biochemical specificity for calcium over other divalent cations
Confirms mineral nature in metabolic bone biopsies and vessels

steps.tx: In older adults, dystrophic calcification commonly targets the aortic valve cusps, producing severe mechanical narrowing of the aortic outflow tract. In **calcific aortic stenosis**, decades of repetitive mechanical shear stress across the valve cusps injure valvular endothelial cells, inciting lipid accumulation, chronic inflammation, and massive nodular calcification that immobilizes the leaflets.
steps.say: Calcific aortic stenosis develops when chronic mechanical shear stresses cause nodular calcification of cusps.

nodes.label: Lifelong Mechanical Flexing and High Shear Stress Injure Aortic Cusps
Circulating Lipoproteins Infiltrate Fibrosa Layer, Inciting Inflammation
Valvular Interstitial Cells Differentiate into Osteoblast-Like Phenotypes
Massive Stony Hard Nodules Precipitate, Restricting Systolic Leaflet Opening
